This can be explained as: the first is governed by an omitted oath particle (wāw al-qasam), its estimated form being ﴿fa-wa-al-ḥaqqi wa-al-ḥaqqi﴾ (so by the truth and the truth), and the second is conjoined to it, as you say: "wa-Allāhi wa-Allāhi la-aqūmanna" (by God, by God, I will surely stand). And ﴿aqūlu﴾ is an interjection (i'tirāḍ) between the oath and its response.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: ﴿wa-al-ḥaqqa aqūlu﴾: that is, "I say nothing except the truth," in the manner of quoting the wording of the thing sworn by. Its meaning is emphasis and affirmation (tawkīd and tasdīd). This aspect is permissible both for the accusative and the nominative, and it is a subtle and good aspect. He ended there.

Its summary is that he made the verb "say" operate on the wording of the thing sworn by, by way of quotation, whether in the accusative, nominative, or genitive. Mujāhid and al-A'mash, with a variant from them both; Abān ibn Taghlib; Ṭalḥa in one narration; Ḥamza, 'Āṣim (according to al-Mufaḍḍal), Khalaf, and al-'Absī read ﴿fa-al-ḥaqqu﴾ in the nominative and ﴿wa-al-ḥaqqa﴾ in the accusative, and their i'rāb (grammatical analysis) has already been mentioned.

The apparent meaning is that His saying ﴿ajma'īna﴾ (all) is an emphasis for the one spoken about and the one conjoined to it, which is the pronoun of Iblīs and whoever is conjoined to him, meaning: "from you and from those who follow you, all of them." Al-Zamakhsharī permitted that ﴿ajma'īna﴾ be an emphasis for the pronoun in ﴿minhum﴾ (from among them) which is implied, meaning: "I will surely fill Jahannam with the devils and with whoever followed them from all of mankind, with no difference in that between one person and another, after the existence of followers among them from the descendants of the prophets and others." He ended there.

The pronoun in ﴿'alayhi﴾ (upon it) refers to the Qur'an, as said by Ibn 'Abbās. It has also been said that it refers to the revelation (waḥy), and it has been said that it refers to the call to God (al-du'ā' ilā Allāh).

﴿wa-mā anā mina al-mutakallifīn﴾ (and I am not of those who impose): that is, those who affect what they are not of, adorning themselves with what is not theirs, so that I would claim prophethood and speak on behalf of God.

﴿in huwa﴾ (it is not), that is, the Qur'an, ﴿illā dhikrun﴾ (except a reminder): that is, from God, ﴿li-al-'ālamīn﴾ (to the worlds): the two weighty creatures, mankind and jinn.

﴿wa-la-ta'lamunna naba'ahu﴾ (and you will surely know its news): that is, the final outcome of its report for whoever believed in it and whoever turned away from it. ﴿ba'da ḥīn﴾ (after a time). Ibn 'Abbās, 'Ikrima, and Ibn Zayd said: it means the Day of Resurrection. Qatāda, al-Farrā', and al-Zajjāj said: after death. Al-Ḥasan used to say: "O son of Adam, at death the certain news (al-khabar al-yaqīn) will come to you." It has also been said: the meaning is that the reality of what I say will become clear to you.

﴿ba'da ḥīn﴾: that is, in the near future, when the swords of the Muslims seize you, and that was the Battle of Badr. Al-Suddī indicated this.

* *

Sūrat al-Zumar: seventy-five verses, Meccan.

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. ﴿The revelation of the Book is from God, the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾ [al-Zumar: 1]. ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, so worship God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-Zumar: 2]. ﴿Unquestionably, to God belongs sincere religion. And those who take protectors other than Him, [say], "We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to God in position." Indeed, God will judge between them concerning that over which they differ. Indeed, God does not guide one who is a liar and [continually] ungrateful﴾ [al-Zumar: 3]. ﴿Had God intended to take a son, He would have chosen from what He creates whatever He wills. Exalted is He. He is God, the One, the Subduer﴾ [al-Zumar: 4]. ﴿He created the heavens and the earth in truth. He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term. Unquestionably, He is the Almighty, the Forgiving﴾ [al-Zumar: 5]. ﴿He created you from one soul; then He made from it its mate, and He sent down for you eight kinds of livestock. He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, in three darknesses. That is God, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion. There is no deity except Him, so how are you turned away?﴾ [al-Zumar: 6]. ﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed God is free of need of you, and He does not approve for His servants disbelief; but if you are grateful, He approves it for you. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the chests﴾ [al-Zumar: 7]. ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance. Then when He bestows upon him a favor from Him, he forgets what he had been calling to before and sets up rivals to God to mislead [others] from His way. Say, "Enjoy your disbelief for a little; indeed, you are of the companions of the Fire"﴾ [al-Zumar: 8]. ﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient during periods of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord [like one who does not]? Say, "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?" Only they will be reminded who are people of understanding﴾ [al-Zumar: 9]. ﴿Say, "O My servants who have believed, fear your Lord. For those who do good in this world is good, and the earth of God is spacious. Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account"﴾ [al-Zumar: 10]. ﴿Say, "Indeed, I have been commanded to worship God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-Zumar: 11]. ﴿And I have been commanded to be the first of the Muslims﴾ [al-Zumar: 12]. ﴿Say, "Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a great Day"﴾ [al-Zumar: 13]. ﴿Say, "It is God I worship, sincere to Him in my religion﴾ [al-Zumar: 14]. ﴿So worship what you will besides Him." Say, "Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss"﴾ [al-Zumar: 15]. ﴿For them will be layers of fire above them and layers below them. That is what God frightens His servants with. O My servants, then fear Me﴾ [al-Zumar: 16]. ﴿And those who avoid the false gods, not worshipping them, and turn back to God—for them is good news. So give good tidings to My servants﴾ [al-Zumar: 17]. ﴿Those who listen to speech and follow the best of it. Those are the ones whom God has guided, and those are the people of understanding﴾ [al-Zumar: 18]. ﴿Then is one upon whom the word of punishment has come [to be deserved]—would you, then, save one who is in the Fire?﴾ [al-Zumar: 19]. ﴿But those who fear their Lord will have lofty chambers, above which are built chambers, beneath which rivers flow. [It is] the promise of God; God does not fail in His promise﴾ [al-Zumar: 20]. ﴿Have you not seen that God sends down rain from the sky and makes it flow as springs in the earth, then brings out by it crops of varying colors? Then it dries, and you see it turn yellow; then He makes it crumbled debris. Indeed, in that is a reminder for those of understanding﴾ [al-Zumar: 21]. ﴿So is one whose breast God has expanded to Islam and who is upon light from his Lord [like one whose heart is hardened]? Woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of God. Those are in manifest error﴾ [al-Zumar: 22]. ﴿God has sent down the best statement, a Book consistent and repeated; the skins shiver therefrom of those who fear their Lord; then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of God. That is the guidance of God; He guides thereby whom He wills. And whom God leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾ [al-Zumar: 23]. ﴿Then is one who shields his face with his face from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection [like one who is safe]? And it will be said to the wrongdoers, "Taste what you used to earn"﴾ [al-Zumar: 24]. ﴿Those before them denied, and the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive﴾ [al-Zumar: 25]. ﴿So God made them taste disgrace in the life of this world, but the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew﴾ [al-Zumar: 26]. ﴿And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example that they might be reminded﴾ [al-Zumar: 27]. ﴿An Arabic Qur'an, without any crookedness, that they might fear God﴾ [al-Zumar: 28]. ﴿God presents an example: a man in whom are [several] partners disputing with one another, and a man belonging exclusively to one man. Are they equal in comparison? Praise is to God; but most of them do not know﴾ [al-Zumar: 29]. ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die﴾ [al-Zumar: 30]. ﴿Then indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord you will dispute﴾ [al-Zumar: 31].

[p. 413] Al-Takwīr: wrapping and coiling. It is said: "kāra al-'imāmata 'alā ra'sihi wa-kawwarahā" (he wound the turban on his head). "Khawwalahu al-ni'mata" means: he gave him a favor at the outset, without any reward; and "khawwala" is not used for a recompense. Zuhayr said:
"There, if they are given wealth as a favor, they are given [wealth] as a favor" (wording variant: "yustakhyalū al-māla yukhayyalū").
Abū al-Najm said:
"He gave and did not withhold, and did not make others withhold; a heap of the summits from the favored property of the bestower."

Hāja al-zar'u: it rose from its roots; it is said: it dried up. Al-ḥuṭām: the crumbs after its dryness. Al-qush'arīra: the contraction of the skin; it is said: "iqsha'arra jiluduhu min al-khawf" (his skin shivered from fear): his hair stood up, and it is a proverb for intense fear. Al-shikāsa: bad character and its difficulty.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 38, verses 67–88 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Say: It is a great news.﴾ ﴿You turn away from it.﴾ ﴿I had no knowledge of the Exalted Assembly when they disputed.﴾ ﴿It is only revealed to me that I am a clear warner.﴾ ﴿When your Lord said to the angels: I am creating a human from clay.﴾ ﴿So when I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down prostrate before him.﴾ ﴿So the angels prostrated, all of them together.﴾ ﴿Except Iblis; he was arrogant and was among the disbelievers.﴾ ﴿He said: O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My two hands? Were you arrogant, or were you among the exalted?﴾ ﴿He said: I am better than him; You created me from fire and You created him from clay.﴾ ﴿He said: Then get out of it, for you are accursed.﴾ ﴿And indeed My curse is upon you until the Day of Recompense.﴾ ﴿He said: My Lord, then give me respite until the Day they are resurrected.﴾ ﴿He said: Then you are among those given respite.﴾ ﴿Until the Day of the appointed time.﴾ ﴿He said: By Your might, I will surely mislead them all.﴾ ﴿Except Your sincere servants among them.﴾ ﴿He said: Then the truth, and I say the truth.﴾ ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you and with whoever follows you of them, all together.﴾ ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any wage for it, and I am not of the pretenders.﴾ ﴿It is only a reminder to the worlds.﴾ ﴿And you will surely know its news after a time.﴾.

The pronoun in His saying ﴿Say: It is a great news﴾ refers to what he had informed of: that he is a messenger warning and calling to Allah, and that He, exalted is He, is the One alone in divinity, characterized by those attributes of oneness, dominion, sovereignty over the world, might and forgiveness. It is a great report, from which none turns away except a heedless person who is extremely heedless.

Ibn Abbas said: "the great news" is the Qur'an. Al-Hasan said: it is the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: it is the story of Adam, and the informing of it without having heard it from anyone.

The author of al-Tahrir said: the context and apparent meaning of the verse indicate that by His saying ﴿Say: It is a great news﴾ He means what Allah related of the dispute of the people of the Fire and the arguing of the followers with the leaders, because it is among the conditions of the resurrection, and the Quraysh used to deny the resurrection, the reckoning and the punishment, and they were turning away from that.

His saying ﴿I had no knowledge of the Exalted Assembly when they disputed﴾ is an argument against the Quraysh that what he brought is from Allah and not from himself. Indeed, whoever is on earth has no knowledge of whoever is in heaven except by Allah's informing; and knowledge of the unseen cannot be reached except by Allah's informing. His knowledge of the conditions of the people of the Fire and the beginning of the creation of Adam was not from himself; so his informing of that is by Allah's informing. The evidence is the story of Adam, because he was the first human created, and between him and the Messenger, peace be upon him, there were long ages and bygone generations. End of the quotation, and at its end there is some abridgment.

Then he argued for the authenticity of his prophethood: that what he reports about the Exalted Assembly and their disputing is a matter of which he had no knowledge at all. Then he came to know it from a route other than the one by which learners acquire knowledge; rather, that is derived from revelation. The phrase "with the assembly" (bi-l-mala') is related to "knowledge" ('ilm), and "when" (idh) is in the accusative governed by it. Al-Zamakhshari said: it is related to a deleted element, because the meaning is: I had no knowledge of the speech of the Exalted Assembly at the time of their disputing.

"When he said" (idh qala) is a substitute (badal) for "when they dispute" (idh yakhtasimun) regarding the Exalted Assembly, who are the angels. Whoever said they are the Quraysh is further from correct. The disputing of the angels concerned the matter of Adam and his offspring, in placing them on the earth. They said: ﴿Will You place therein one who causes corruption therein?﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:30]. Ibn Abbas said: and al-Hasan said: Indeed Allah creates a creation that we were nobler than and more knowledgeable than. It was also said: it concerned the expiations and forgiveness of sins; for when a servant does a good deed, the angels differ about the measure of its reward in that, until Allah decides as He wills. And in a hadith: "His Lord said to him in his sleep, peace be upon him: 'About what do they dispute?' I said: 'I do not know.' He said: 'About the expiations, and about perfecting the ablution in hardships, and about walking the steps to the congregations.'"

Al-Zamakhshari said: the speaking between Allah, glory be to Him, and the other was through an angel, and the actual speaker was the intermediary angel. So it is valid that the speaking was between the angels and Adam and Iblis, and they are the Exalted Assembly.

The meaning of the disputing is speaking back and forth. It was said: the Exalted Assembly are the angels, and the pronoun in ﴿when they dispute﴾ refers to the disbelieving Arabs, some of whom say: they are the daughters of Allah, and some say: they are gods that are worshipped, and other statements of theirs.

﴿It is only revealed to me﴾, i.e., only what is revealed to me; ﴿that I am a warner﴾, i.e., for warning. He omitted the preposition (lam), and joined the verb to its object, the passive form. The pronoun may be implied by the meaning: i.e., "It is revealed to me" refers to it, meaning: only the warning is revealed, and "to me" is put in its place. It may also be that "innama" is the passive subject: i.e., only the warning is revealed to me. Abu Ja'far read ﴿illa innama﴾ with a kasra on the hamza of innama, as a reported speech (hikaya): meaning, only this sentence is revealed to me, as if it were said to him: "You are a clear warner," and he related the meaning. This is like a person saying: "I am knowledgeable," and it is said to him: "You said that you are knowledgeable," so the meaning is reported.

Al-Zamakhshari said: It was also read innama with a kasra as reported speech, i.e., only this statement, which is that I say to you ﴿Indeed I am a clear warner﴾, so I do not claim anything else. End of quotation.

In his explanation there is a contradiction, for he said "i.e., only this statement," which apparently is the sentence ﴿Indeed I am a clear warner﴾, then he said: "which is that I say to you," so the position is that of the subject, namely "that I say to you," and "that" and what follows are in the accusative position. According to his statement "only this statement," it would be in the nominative position, so they conflict.

It has been mentioned that "when he said" is a substitute for "when they dispute," this being if the dispute was about the one who will be made successor on earth; but according to other statements it would be in the accusative governed by "mention" (udhkur).

Since the Quraysh opposed the Messenger, peace be upon him, out of envy and arrogance, He mentioned the situation of Iblis, who opposed the command of Allah out of envy and arrogance, and what he came to of cursing and expulsion from the mercy of Allah, so that whoever has some trait of these two would be deterred from that.

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you say: how was it valid for Him to say to them ﴿Indeed I am creating a human﴾, when they did not know what a human is and had not been acquainted with it before? I say: its explanation is that He had said to them: "Indeed I am creating a creation of such and such a description," but when He related it He limited Himself to the name. End of quotation.

The human (bashar) is Adam, peace be upon him. Here He mentions that He created him from clay; and in Al 'Imran: ﴿He created him from dust﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:59]; in al-Hijr: ﴿from dry clay of black molded mud﴾ [al-Hijr 15:26]; and in al-Anbiya': ﴿from haste﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:37]. There is no contradiction, since the remote substance is dust, then what follows it, which is clay, then what follows it, which is black molded mud, then the substance that follows the mud, which is dry clay. As for ﴿from haste﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:37], its explanation has already passed.

﴿So when I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down prostrate before him.﴾ ﴿So the angels prostrated, all of them together.﴾ ﴿Except Iblis﴾: the discussion of this has already been covered in al-Hijr. Here ﴿he was arrogant and was among the disbelievers﴾, [p. 410] and in al-Baqarah: ﴿He refused and was arrogant and was among the disbelievers﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:34]; in al-A'raf: ﴿He was not among those who prostrate﴾ [al-A'raf 7:11]; in al-Hijr: ﴿He refused to be with those who prostrate﴾ [al-Hijr 15:31]; in al-Isra': ﴿He said: Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?﴾ [al-Isra' 17:61]; and in al-Kahf: ﴿He was of the jinn and defied the command of his Lord﴾ [al-Kahf 18:50].

The exception in all these verses indicates that he did not prostrate. Sometimes it is emphasized with pure negation; sometimes his refusal to prostrate is mentioned, which is his disdain for that; and sometimes it is stated explicitly that this refusal was caused by arrogance. The apparent meaning is that His saying ﴿and was among the disbelievers﴾ means his disbelief at that time, even if he had not been a disbeliever before; and it is conjoined to "was arrogant," which strengthens this, because the arrogance about prostration only occurred to him at the time of the command.

It is also possible that it is information from Him about his disbelief having preceded in past times in the knowledge of Allah.

﴿He said: O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating﴾. In al-A'raf: ﴿What prevented you from not prostrating﴾ [al-A'raf 7:12]. This indicates that "an tasjuda" here shows that "la" in ﴿an la aqula﴾ [al-A'raf 7:105] is extra; and the meaning also indicates this, because He only asks about what prevented him from prostrating, and this is a question of confirmation and rebuke. As for "li-ma khalaqtu" [what I created], those who permit applying "ma" to individuals who have intellect have used it as evidence, and they interpreted "ma" here as a verbal noun (masdariyyah), and the verbal noun is intended to mean the created thing, not the literal verbal noun.

Al-Jahdari read ﴿lamma﴾ with a fatha on the lam and a shadda on the mim, ﴿khalaqtu bi-yadayya﴾ in the singular; the majority read it in the dual. It is also read ﴿biyadayya﴾ like the reading ﴿bi-musrikhiyya﴾ [Ibrahim 14:22]. He, exalted is He, also said: ﴿of what Our hands have done﴾ [Ya Sin 36:71] in the plural. All of these are expressions for power and strength; and He expressed it with "hand," since it is customary among humans that seizing and strength are by the hand.

Al-Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-Tayyib held that the hand is an attribute of essence (sifat dhat). Ibn Atiyya said: this is an opinion that is disliked.

The majority read ﴿asta'kbarta﴾ with the interrogative hamza, so "am" is a connected "am" that is equivalent to the hamza. Ibn Atiyya said: many grammarians held that "am" is not equivalent to the alif when the two verbs differ; it is only equivalent when both are attached to one verb, like your saying: "Did Zayd stand or 'Amr?" and "Did Zayd stand or 'Amr?" When the verbs differ, as in this verse, it is not equivalent. The meaning of the verse is: Has arrogance now come to you, or were you formerly one for whom it is not fitting to be commanded with such, because of the height of your station? This is by way of rebuke. End of quotation.

What he mentioned from many grammarians is an incorrect doctrine. Sibawayh said: you say "Did you strike Zayd or did you kill him?" Beginning here with the verb is better, because you are only asking about one of them, not knowing which of them occurred, and you are not asking about the position of one of them, as if you said: "Which of those occurred?" End of quotation. So he made "am" equivalent to the alif even though the two verbs differ.

﴿from among the exalted﴾: from among those who have risen and surpassed. So he answered that he was among the exalted, when he said ﴿I am better than him﴾. It was said: Have you now become arrogant, or have you not ceased, since you were, to be among the arrogant? The meaning of the hamza is affirmation. End of quotation.

A group, including Ibn Kathir and others, read ﴿astakbarta﴾ with the alif connected, which is the reading of the people of Makkah, and it is not in the well-known transmission of Ibn Kathir. It is possible that the interrogative hamza was deleted because "am" indicates it, as in the poet's words: "With seven you threw the coals, or with eight?" It is also possible that it is a statement that He addressed to him in the manner of rebuke. "Am" may be disjunctive (munqati'ah), and the meaning is: Rather, you are among the exalted in your own eyes, belittling him.

﴿He said: I am better than him; You created me from fire and You created him from clay.﴾ The discussion of this has already passed in al-A'raf.

﴿He said: Then get out of it﴾ up to His saying ﴿until the Day of the appointed time﴾: the discussion of something like this has already passed in al-Hijr, except that here it says ﴿My curse﴾, and there the word is "the curse," which is more general. Do you not see His saying: ﴿Those are cursed by Allah, and the cursers curse them﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:159]? As for the construction with the possessive suffix, the generality in "curse" is more general; curses arise because whoever is under the curse of Allah is also under the curse of every curser. This is from the perspective of meaning; but as to the wording, it requires specification.

﴿He said: By Your might, I will surely mislead them﴾: Iblis swore here by the might of Allah. In al-A'raf he said: ﴿Because You have led me astray, I will surely sit in wait﴾ [al-A'raf 7:16]; and in al-Hijr: ﴿My Lord, because You have led me astray, I will surely make evil seem attractive to them﴾ [al-Hijr 15:39]. The discussion of these two has already passed in their places. Some exegetes said that the preposition in ﴿bima aghwaytani﴾ [al-Hijr 15:39] and in ﴿fabima aghwaytani﴾ [al-A'raf 7:16] is not the oath particle. If it is the oath particle, then it occurs in three places: here ﴿la-ughwiyannahum﴾, in al-A'raf ﴿la-aq'udanna﴾ [al-A'raf 7:16], and in al-Hijr ﴿la-uzayyinanna﴾ [al-Hijr 15:39].

[p. 411] The majority of readers recited ﴿fa-al-ḥaqqa wa-al-ḥaqqa﴾ with both words in the accusative (naṣb). As for the first, it is the thing sworn by, and the particle of oath has been omitted from it, as in his saying: "amānata Allāhi la-aqūmanna" (I swear by the trust of God that I will surely stand). The thing sworn to is ﴿la-amla'anna﴾ (I will surely fill).

﴿wa-al-ḥaqqa aqūlu﴾ (And the truth I say) is a parenthetical insertion (i'tirāḍ, an interjected clause) between the oath and its response. Al-Zamakhsharī said: its meaning is "I say nothing except the truth," and he ended there, because according to him the fronting of the object (taqaddum al-maf'ūl) indicates restriction (ḥaṣr). The truth that is sworn by is either God's name, which is in His saying ﴿inna Allāha huwa al-ḥaqqu al-mubīn﴾ [al-Nūr: 25] (Indeed, God is the manifest Truth), or it is the opposite of falsehood (al-bāṭil). It has also been said that ﴿fa-al-ḥaqqu﴾ is in the accusative as an incitement (ighrā', urging or warning), meaning: "Hold fast to the truth," and ﴿la-amla'anna﴾ is the response of an omitted oath. Al-Farrā' said: it is in the sense of your saying "ḥaqqan lā shakka" (truly, without doubt), and the presence or omission of the definite article (alif-lām) is the same, meaning: "I will surely fill Jahannam truly." He ended there.

This verbal noun (maṣdar) that comes as an emphasis (ta'kīd) on the content of the sentence may not be placed first according to the majority of grammarians, and that is restricted to a sentence whose two parts are definite and fixed in their definiteness.

The author of al-Basīṭ said: It may be that the predicate (khabar) is indefinite. He said: the subject (mubtada', topic) may be a pronoun, such as: "huwa Zaydun ma'rūfan" (he is Zayd, well known), "wa-huwa al-ḥaqqu bayyinan" (and he is the truth, clear), and "anā al-amīru mufakhiran" (I am the commander, boasting); and it may be a noun, as in your saying: "Zaydun abūka 'aṭūfan" (Zayd is your father, affectionate), and "akhūka Zaydun ma'rūfan" (your brother is Zayd, well known). He ended there.

The Arabs said: "Zaydun qā'imun ghayra dhī shakkin" (Zayd is standing, without any doubt). So the ḥāl (circumstantial clause) came after a sentence whose predicate is indefinite, and it is an emphatic circumstantial phrase for the content of the sentence. It seems that al-Farrā' did not stipulate what our fellow scholars mentioned, namely that the subject and predicate must be known and fixed, because there is no difference between emphasizing the content of a nominal sentence and emphasizing a verbal sentence.

It has also been said: the underlying form is ﴿fa-al-ḥaqqu al-ḥaqqu﴾, meaning: "I will do it." Ibn 'Abbās, Mujāhid, and al-A'mash read both words in the nominative (raf'), so the first is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is omitted. It has been said that its estimated form is ﴿fa-al-ḥaqqu anā﴾ (so the truth is I), and it has been said: ﴿fa-al-ḥaqqu minnī﴾ (so the truth is from me), and it has been said: its estimated form is ﴿fa-al-ḥaqqu qasamī﴾ (so the truth is my oath), and it was omitted just as it was omitted in "la'amruka la-aqūmanna" (by your life, I will surely stand), and in "yamīnu Allāhi abraḥu qā'idan" (the oath of God, I will not leave while seated), meaning: "la'amruka qasamī" (by your life is my oath) and "yamīnu Allāhi qasamī" (the oath of God is my oath). This sentence is the sentence of the oath, and its response is ﴿la-amla'anna﴾.

As for ﴿wa-al-ḥaqqu aqūlu﴾, it is also a subject, whose predicate is the sentence, and the returning pronoun (al-'ā'id) was omitted, as in the reading of Ibn 'Abbās: ﴿wa-kullan wa'ada Allāhu al-ḥusnā﴾ [al-Nisā': 95] (And to each God has promised the best). Ibn 'Aṭiyya said: As for the first, it is raised by being the subject, and its predicate is in His saying ﴿la-amla'anna﴾, because the meaning is: "that I will fill." He ended there.

This is not correct, because ﴿la-amla'anna﴾ is the response of an oath, and it must be a sentence, so it cannot be interpreted as a single word (mufrad). Also, it is not a verbal noun estimated with a verbal particle and a verb so that it could be resolved into them. But since it was valid for him to attribute what was estimated to the subject, it was judged to be its predicate.

Al-Ḥasan, 'Īsā, and 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Ḥammād, from Abū Bakr, read both words in the genitive (jarr). This can be explained as: the first is governed by an omitted oath particle (wāw al-qasam), its estimated form being ﴿fa-wa-al-ḥaqqi wa-al-ḥaqqi﴾ (so by the truth and the truth), and the second is conjoined to it, as you say: "wa-Allāhi wa-Allāhi la-aqūmanna" (by God, by God, I will surely stand). And ﴿aqūlu﴾ is an interjection (i'tirāḍ) between the oath and its response.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: ﴿wa-al-ḥaqqa aqūlu﴾: that is, "I say nothing except the truth," in the manner of quoting the wording of the thing sworn by. Its meaning is emphasis and affirmation (tawkīd and tasdīd). This aspect is permissible both for the accusative and the nominative, and it is a subtle and good aspect. He ended there.

Its summary is that he made the verb "say" operate on the wording of the thing sworn by, by way of quotation, whether in the accusative, nominative, or genitive. Mujāhid and al-A'mash, with a variant from them both; Abān ibn Taghlib; Ṭalḥa in one narration; Ḥamza, 'Āṣim (according to al-Mufaḍḍal), Khalaf, and al-'Absī read ﴿fa-al-ḥaqqu﴾ in the nominative and ﴿wa-al-ḥaqqa﴾ in the accusative, and their i'rāb (grammatical analysis) has already been mentioned.

The apparent meaning is that His saying ﴿ajma'īna﴾ (all) is an emphasis for the one spoken about and the one conjoined to it, which is the pronoun of Iblīs and whoever is conjoined to him, meaning: "from you and from those who follow you, all of them." Al-Zamakhsharī permitted that ﴿ajma'īna﴾ be an emphasis for the pronoun in ﴿minhum﴾ (from among them) which is implied, meaning: "I will surely fill Jahannam with the devils and with whoever followed them from all of mankind, with no difference in that between one person and another, after the existence of followers among them from the descendants of the prophets and others." He ended there.

The pronoun in ﴿'alayhi﴾ (upon it) refers to the Qur'an, as said by Ibn 'Abbās. It has also been said that it refers to the revelation (waḥy), and it has been said that it refers to the call to God (al-du'ā' ilā Allāh).

﴿wa-mā anā mina al-mutakallifīn﴾ (and I am not of those who impose): that is, those who affect what they are not of, adorning themselves with what is not theirs, so that I would claim prophethood and speak on behalf of God.

﴿in huwa﴾ (it is not), that is, the Qur'an, ﴿illā dhikrun﴾ (except a reminder): that is, from God, ﴿li-al-'ālamīn﴾ (to the worlds): the two weighty creatures, mankind and jinn.

﴿wa-la-ta'lamunna naba'ahu﴾ (and you will surely know its news): that is, the final outcome of its report for whoever believed in it and whoever turned away from it. ﴿ba'da ḥīn﴾ (after a time). Ibn 'Abbās, 'Ikrima, and Ibn Zayd said: it means the Day of Resurrection. Qatāda, al-Farrā', and al-Zajjāj said: after death. Al-Ḥasan used to say: "O son of Adam, at death the certain news (al-khabar al-yaqīn) will come to you." It has also been said: the meaning is that the reality of what I say will become clear to you.

﴿ba'da ḥīn﴾: that is, in the near future, when the swords of the Muslims seize you, and that was the Battle of Badr. Al-Suddī indicated this.

* *

Sūrat al-Zumar: seventy-five verses, Meccan.

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. ﴿The revelation of the Book is from God, the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾ [al-Zumar: 1]. ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, so worship God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-Zumar: 2]. ﴿Unquestionably, to God belongs sincere religion. And those who take protectors other than Him, [say], "We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to God in position." Indeed, God will judge between them concerning that over which they differ. Indeed, God does not guide one who is a liar and [continually] ungrateful﴾ [al-Zumar: 3]. ﴿Had God intended to take a son, He would have chosen from what He creates whatever He wills. Exalted is He. He is God, the One, the Subduer﴾ [al-Zumar: 4]. ﴿He created the heavens and the earth in truth. He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term. Unquestionably, He is the Almighty, the Forgiving﴾ [al-Zumar: 5]. ﴿He created you from one soul; then He made from it its mate, and He sent down for you eight kinds of livestock. He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, in three darknesses. That is God, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion. There is no deity except Him, so how are you turned away?﴾ [al-Zumar: 6]. ﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed God is free of need of you, and He does not approve for His servants disbelief; but if you are grateful, He approves it for you. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the chests﴾ [al-Zumar: 7]. ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance. Then when He bestows upon him a favor from Him, he forgets what he had been calling to before and sets up rivals to God to mislead [others] from His way. Say, "Enjoy your disbelief for a little; indeed, you are of the companions of the Fire"﴾ [al-Zumar: 8]. ﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient during periods of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord [like one who does not]? Say, "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?" Only they will be reminded who are people of understanding﴾ [al-Zumar: 9]. ﴿Say, "O My servants who have believed, fear your Lord. For those who do good in this world is good, and the earth of God is spacious. Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account"﴾ [al-Zumar: 10]. ﴿Say, "Indeed, I have been commanded to worship God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-Zumar: 11]. ﴿And I have been commanded to be the first of the Muslims﴾ [al-Zumar: 12]. ﴿Say, "Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a great Day"﴾ [al-Zumar: 13]. ﴿Say, "It is God I worship, sincere to Him in my religion﴾ [al-Zumar: 14]. ﴿So worship what you will besides Him." Say, "Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss"﴾ [al-Zumar: 15]. ﴿For them will be layers of fire above them and layers below them. That is what God frightens His servants with. O My servants, then fear Me﴾ [al-Zumar: 16]. ﴿And those who avoid the false gods, not worshipping them, and turn back to God—for them is good news. So give good tidings to My servants﴾ [al-Zumar: 17]. ﴿Those who listen to speech and follow the best of it. Those are the ones whom God has guided, and those are the people of understanding﴾ [al-Zumar: 18]. ﴿Then is one upon whom the word of punishment has come [to be deserved]—would you, then, save one who is in the Fire?﴾ [al-Zumar: 19]. ﴿But those who fear their Lord will have lofty chambers, above which are built chambers, beneath which rivers flow. [It is] the promise of God; God does not fail in His promise﴾ [al-Zumar: 20]. ﴿Have you not seen that God sends down rain from the sky and makes it flow as springs in the earth, then brings out by it crops of varying colors? Then it dries, and you see it turn yellow; then He makes it crumbled debris. Indeed, in that is a reminder for those of understanding﴾ [al-Zumar: 21]. ﴿So is one whose breast God has expanded to Islam and who is upon light from his Lord [like one whose heart is hardened]? Woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of God. Those are in manifest error﴾ [al-Zumar: 22]. ﴿God has sent down the best statement, a Book consistent and repeated; the skins shiver therefrom of those who fear their Lord; then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of God. That is the guidance of God; He guides thereby whom He wills. And whom God leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾ [al-Zumar: 23]. ﴿Then is one who shields his face with his face from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection [like one who is safe]? And it will be said to the wrongdoers, "Taste what you used to earn"﴾ [al-Zumar: 24]. ﴿Those before them denied, and the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive﴾ [al-Zumar: 25]. ﴿So God made them taste disgrace in the life of this world, but the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew﴾ [al-Zumar: 26]. ﴿And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example that they might be reminded﴾ [al-Zumar: 27]. ﴿An Arabic Qur'an, without any crookedness, that they might fear God﴾ [al-Zumar: 28]. ﴿God presents an example: a man in whom are [several] partners disputing with one another, and a man belonging exclusively to one man. Are they equal in comparison? Praise is to God; but most of them do not know﴾ [al-Zumar: 29]. ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die﴾ [al-Zumar: 30]. ﴿Then indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord you will dispute﴾ [al-Zumar: 31].

[p. 413] Al-Takwīr: wrapping and coiling. It is said: "kāra al-'imāmata 'alā ra'sihi wa-kawwarahā" (he wound the turban on his head). "Khawwalahu al-ni'mata" means: he gave him a favor at the outset, without any reward; and "khawwala" is not used for a recompense. Zuhayr said:
"There, if they are given wealth as a favor, they are given [wealth] as a favor" (wording variant: "yustakhyalū al-māla yukhayyalū").
Abū al-Najm said:
"He gave and did not withhold, and did not make others withhold; a heap of the summits from the favored property of the bestower."

Hāja al-zar'u: it rose from its roots; it is said: it dried up. Al-ḥuṭām: the crumbs after its dryness. Al-qush'arīra: the contraction of the skin; it is said: "iqsha'arra jiluduhu min al-khawf" (his skin shivered from fear): his hair stood up, and it is a proverb for intense fear. Al-shikāsa: bad character and its difficulty.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 38, verses 67–88 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Say: It is a great news.﴾ ﴿You turn away from it.﴾ ﴿I had no knowledge of the Exalted Assembly when they disputed.﴾ ﴿It is only revealed to me that I am a clear warner.﴾ ﴿When your Lord said to the angels: I am creating a human from clay.﴾ ﴿So when I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down prostrate before him.﴾ ﴿So the angels prostrated, all of them together.﴾ ﴿Except Iblis; he was arrogant and was among the disbelievers.﴾ ﴿He said: O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My two hands? Were you arrogant, or were you among the exalted?﴾ ﴿He said: I am better than him; You created me from fire and You created him from clay.﴾ ﴿He said: Then get out of it, for you are accursed.﴾ ﴿And indeed My curse is upon you until the Day of Recompense.﴾ ﴿He said: My Lord, then give me respite until the Day they are resurrected.﴾ ﴿He said: Then you are among those given respite.﴾ ﴿Until the Day of the appointed time.﴾ ﴿He said: By Your might, I will surely mislead them all.﴾ ﴿Except Your sincere servants among them.﴾ ﴿He said: Then the truth, and I say the truth.﴾ ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you and with whoever follows you of them, all together.﴾ ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any wage for it, and I am not of the pretenders.﴾ ﴿It is only a reminder to the worlds.﴾ ﴿And you will surely know its news after a time.﴾.

The pronoun in His saying ﴿Say: It is a great news﴾ refers to what he had informed of: that he is a messenger warning and calling to Allah, and that He, exalted is He, is the One alone in divinity, characterized by those attributes of oneness, dominion, sovereignty over the world, might and forgiveness. It is a great report, from which none turns away except a heedless person who is extremely heedless.

Ibn Abbas said: "the great news" is the Qur'an. Al-Hasan said: it is the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: it is the story of Adam, and the informing of it without having heard it from anyone.

The author of al-Tahrir said: the context and apparent meaning of the verse indicate that by His saying ﴿Say: It is a great news﴾ He means what Allah related of the dispute of the people of the Fire and the arguing of the followers with the leaders, because it is among the conditions of the resurrection, and the Quraysh used to deny the resurrection, the reckoning and the punishment, and they were turning away from that.

His saying ﴿I had no knowledge of the Exalted Assembly when they disputed﴾ is an argument against the Quraysh that what he brought is from Allah and not from himself. Indeed, whoever is on earth has no knowledge of whoever is in heaven except by Allah's informing; and knowledge of the unseen cannot be reached except by Allah's informing. His knowledge of the conditions of the people of the Fire and the beginning of the creation of Adam was not from himself; so his informing of that is by Allah's informing. The evidence is the story of Adam, because he was the first human created, and between him and the Messenger, peace be upon him, there were long ages and bygone generations. End of the quotation, and at its end there is some abridgment.

Then he argued for the authenticity of his prophethood: that what he reports about the Exalted Assembly and their disputing is a matter of which he had no knowledge at all. Then he came to know it from a route other than the one by which learners acquire knowledge; rather, that is derived from revelation. The phrase "with the assembly" (bi-l-mala') is related to "knowledge" ('ilm), and "when" (idh) is in the accusative governed by it. Al-Zamakhshari said: it is related to a deleted element, because the meaning is: I had no knowledge of the speech of the Exalted Assembly at the time of their disputing.

"When he said" (idh qala) is a substitute (badal) for "when they dispute" (idh yakhtasimun) regarding the Exalted Assembly, who are the angels. Whoever said they are the Quraysh is further from correct. The disputing of the angels concerned the matter of Adam and his offspring, in placing them on the earth. They said: ﴿Will You place therein one who causes corruption therein?﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:30]. Ibn Abbas said: and al-Hasan said: Indeed Allah creates a creation that we were nobler than and more knowledgeable than. It was also said: it concerned the expiations and forgiveness of sins; for when a servant does a good deed, the angels differ about the measure of its reward in that, until Allah decides as He wills. And in a hadith: "His Lord said to him in his sleep, peace be upon him: 'About what do they dispute?' I said: 'I do not know.' He said: 'About the expiations, and about perfecting the ablution in hardships, and about walking the steps to the congregations.'"

Al-Zamakhshari said: the speaking between Allah, glory be to Him, and the other was through an angel, and the actual speaker was the intermediary angel. So it is valid that the speaking was between the angels and Adam and Iblis, and they are the Exalted Assembly.

The meaning of the disputing is speaking back and forth. It was said: the Exalted Assembly are the angels, and the pronoun in ﴿when they dispute﴾ refers to the disbelieving Arabs, some of whom say: they are the daughters of Allah, and some say: they are gods that are worshipped, and other statements of theirs.

﴿It is only revealed to me﴾, i.e., only what is revealed to me; ﴿that I am a warner﴾, i.e., for warning. He omitted the preposition (lam), and joined the verb to its object, the passive form. The pronoun may be implied by the meaning: i.e., "It is revealed to me" refers to it, meaning: only the warning is revealed, and "to me" is put in its place. It may also be that "innama" is the passive subject: i.e., only the warning is revealed to me. Abu Ja'far read ﴿illa innama﴾ with a kasra on the hamza of innama, as a reported speech (hikaya): meaning, only this sentence is revealed to me, as if it were said to him: "You are a clear warner," and he related the meaning. This is like a person saying: "I am knowledgeable," and it is said to him: "You said that you are knowledgeable," so the meaning is reported.

Al-Zamakhshari said: It was also read innama with a kasra as reported speech, i.e., only this statement, which is that I say to you ﴿Indeed I am a clear warner﴾, so I do not claim anything else. End of quotation.

In his explanation there is a contradiction, for he said "i.e., only this statement," which apparently is the sentence ﴿Indeed I am a clear warner﴾, then he said: "which is that I say to you," so the position is that of the subject, namely "that I say to you," and "that" and what follows are in the accusative position. According to his statement "only this statement," it would be in the nominative position, so they conflict.

It has been mentioned that "when he said" is a substitute for "when they dispute," this being if the dispute was about the one who will be made successor on earth; but according to other statements it would be in the accusative governed by "mention" (udhkur).

Since the Quraysh opposed the Messenger, peace be upon him, out of envy and arrogance, He mentioned the situation of Iblis, who opposed the command of Allah out of envy and arrogance, and what he came to of cursing and expulsion from the mercy of Allah, so that whoever has some trait of these two would be deterred from that.

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you say: how was it valid for Him to say to them ﴿Indeed I am creating a human﴾, when they did not know what a human is and had not been acquainted with it before? I say: its explanation is that He had said to them: "Indeed I am creating a creation of such and such a description," but when He related it He limited Himself to the name. End of quotation.

The human (bashar) is Adam, peace be upon him. Here He mentions that He created him from clay; and in Al 'Imran: ﴿He created him from dust﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:59]; in al-Hijr: ﴿from dry clay of black molded mud﴾ [al-Hijr 15:26]; and in al-Anbiya': ﴿from haste﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:37]. There is no contradiction, since the remote substance is dust, then what follows it, which is clay, then what follows it, which is black molded mud, then the substance that follows the mud, which is dry clay. As for ﴿from haste﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:37], its explanation has already passed.

﴿So when I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down prostrate before him.﴾ ﴿So the angels prostrated, all of them together.﴾ ﴿Except Iblis﴾: the discussion of this has already been covered in al-Hijr. Here ﴿he was arrogant and was among the disbelievers﴾, [p. 410] and in al-Baqarah: ﴿He refused and was arrogant and was among the disbelievers﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:34]; in al-A'raf: ﴿He was not among those who prostrate﴾ [al-A'raf 7:11]; in al-Hijr: ﴿He refused to be with those who prostrate﴾ [al-Hijr 15:31]; in al-Isra': ﴿He said: Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?﴾ [al-Isra' 17:61]; and in al-Kahf: ﴿He was of the jinn and defied the command of his Lord﴾ [al-Kahf 18:50].

The exception in all these verses indicates that he did not prostrate. Sometimes it is emphasized with pure negation; sometimes his refusal to prostrate is mentioned, which is his disdain for that; and sometimes it is stated explicitly that this refusal was caused by arrogance. The apparent meaning is that His saying ﴿and was among the disbelievers﴾ means his disbelief at that time, even if he had not been a disbeliever before; and it is conjoined to "was arrogant," which strengthens this, because the arrogance about prostration only occurred to him at the time of the command.

It is also possible that it is information from Him about his disbelief having preceded in past times in the knowledge of Allah.

﴿He said: O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating﴾. In al-A'raf: ﴿What prevented you from not prostrating﴾ [al-A'raf 7:12]. This indicates that "an tasjuda" here shows that "la" in ﴿an la aqula﴾ [al-A'raf 7:105] is extra; and the meaning also indicates this, because He only asks about what prevented him from prostrating, and this is a question of confirmation and rebuke. As for "li-ma khalaqtu" [what I created], those who permit applying "ma" to individuals who have intellect have used it as evidence, and they interpreted "ma" here as a verbal noun (masdariyyah), and the verbal noun is intended to mean the created thing, not the literal verbal noun.

Al-Jahdari read ﴿lamma﴾ with a fatha on the lam and a shadda on the mim, ﴿khalaqtu bi-yadayya﴾ in the singular; the majority read it in the dual. It is also read ﴿biyadayya﴾ like the reading ﴿bi-musrikhiyya﴾ [Ibrahim 14:22]. He, exalted is He, also said: ﴿of what Our hands have done﴾ [Ya Sin 36:71] in the plural. All of these are expressions for power and strength; and He expressed it with "hand," since it is customary among humans that seizing and strength are by the hand.

Al-Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-Tayyib held that the hand is an attribute of essence (sifat dhat). Ibn Atiyya said: this is an opinion that is disliked.

The majority read ﴿asta'kbarta﴾ with the interrogative hamza, so "am" is a connected "am" that is equivalent to the hamza. Ibn Atiyya said: many grammarians held that "am" is not equivalent to the alif when the two verbs differ; it is only equivalent when both are attached to one verb, like your saying: "Did Zayd stand or 'Amr?" and "Did Zayd stand or 'Amr?" When the verbs differ, as in this verse, it is not equivalent. The meaning of the verse is: Has arrogance now come to you, or were you formerly one for whom it is not fitting to be commanded with such, because of the height of your station? This is by way of rebuke. End of quotation.

What he mentioned from many grammarians is an incorrect doctrine. Sibawayh said: you say "Did you strike Zayd or did you kill him?" Beginning here with the verb is better, because you are only asking about one of them, not knowing which of them occurred, and you are not asking about the position of one of them, as if you said: "Which of those occurred?" End of quotation. So he made "am" equivalent to the alif even though the two verbs differ.

﴿from among the exalted﴾: from among those who have risen and surpassed. So he answered that he was among the exalted, when he said ﴿I am better than him﴾. It was said: Have you now become arrogant, or have you not ceased, since you were, to be among the arrogant? The meaning of the hamza is affirmation. End of quotation.

A group, including Ibn Kathir and others, read ﴿astakbarta﴾ with the alif connected, which is the reading of the people of Makkah, and it is not in the well-known transmission of Ibn Kathir. It is possible that the interrogative hamza was deleted because "am" indicates it, as in the poet's words: "With seven you threw the coals, or with eight?" It is also possible that it is a statement that He addressed to him in the manner of rebuke. "Am" may be disjunctive (munqati'ah), and the meaning is: Rather, you are among the exalted in your own eyes, belittling him.

﴿He said: I am better than him; You created me from fire and You created him from clay.﴾ The discussion of this has already passed in al-A'raf.

﴿He said: Then get out of it﴾ up to His saying ﴿until the Day of the appointed time﴾: the discussion of something like this has already passed in al-Hijr, except that here it says ﴿My curse﴾, and there the word is "the curse," which is more general. Do you not see His saying: ﴿Those are cursed by Allah, and the cursers curse them﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:159]? As for the construction with the possessive suffix, the generality in "curse" is more general; curses arise because whoever is under the curse of Allah is also under the curse of every curser. This is from the perspective of meaning; but as to the wording, it requires specification.

﴿He said: By Your might, I will surely mislead them﴾: Iblis swore here by the might of Allah. In al-A'raf he said: ﴿Because You have led me astray, I will surely sit in wait﴾ [al-A'raf 7:16]; and in al-Hijr: ﴿My Lord, because You have led me astray, I will surely make evil seem attractive to them﴾ [al-Hijr 15:39]. The discussion of these two has already passed in their places. Some exegetes said that the preposition in ﴿bima aghwaytani﴾ [al-Hijr 15:39] and in ﴿fabima aghwaytani﴾ [al-A'raf 7:16] is not the oath particle. If it is the oath particle, then it occurs in three places: here ﴿la-ughwiyannahum﴾, in al-A'raf ﴿la-aq'udanna﴾ [al-A'raf 7:16], and in al-Hijr ﴿la-uzayyinanna﴾ [al-Hijr 15:39].

[p. 411] The majority of readers recited ﴿fa-al-ḥaqqa wa-al-ḥaqqa﴾ with both words in the accusative (naṣb). As for the first, it is the thing sworn by, and the particle of oath has been omitted from it, as in his saying: "amānata Allāhi la-aqūmanna" (I swear by the trust of God that I will surely stand). The thing sworn to is ﴿la-amla'anna﴾ (I will surely fill).

﴿wa-al-ḥaqqa aqūlu﴾ (And the truth I say) is a parenthetical insertion (i'tirāḍ, an interjected clause) between the oath and its response. Al-Zamakhsharī said: its meaning is "I say nothing except the truth," and he ended there, because according to him the fronting of the object (taqaddum al-maf'ūl) indicates restriction (ḥaṣr). The truth that is sworn by is either God's name, which is in His saying ﴿inna Allāha huwa al-ḥaqqu al-mubīn﴾ [al-Nūr: 25] (Indeed, God is the manifest Truth), or it is the opposite of falsehood (al-bāṭil). It has also been said that ﴿fa-al-ḥaqqu﴾ is in the accusative as an incitement (ighrā', urging or warning), meaning: "Hold fast to the truth," and ﴿la-amla'anna﴾ is the response of an omitted oath. Al-Farrā' said: it is in the sense of your saying "ḥaqqan lā shakka" (truly, without doubt), and the presence or omission of the definite article (alif-lām) is the same, meaning: "I will surely fill Jahannam truly." He ended there.

This verbal noun (maṣdar) that comes as an emphasis (ta'kīd) on the content of the sentence may not be placed first according to the majority of grammarians, and that is restricted to a sentence whose two parts are definite and fixed in their definiteness.

The author of al-Basīṭ said: It may be that the predicate (khabar) is indefinite. He said: the subject (mubtada', topic) may be a pronoun, such as: "huwa Zaydun ma'rūfan" (he is Zayd, well known), "wa-huwa al-ḥaqqu bayyinan" (and he is the truth, clear), and "anā al-amīru mufakhiran" (I am the commander, boasting); and it may be a noun, as in your saying: "Zaydun abūka 'aṭūfan" (Zayd is your father, affectionate), and "akhūka Zaydun ma'rūfan" (your brother is Zayd, well known). He ended there.

The Arabs said: "Zaydun qā'imun ghayra dhī shakkin" (Zayd is standing, without any doubt). So the ḥāl (circumstantial clause) came after a sentence whose predicate is indefinite, and it is an emphatic circumstantial phrase for the content of the sentence. It seems that al-Farrā' did not stipulate what our fellow scholars mentioned, namely that the subject and predicate must be known and fixed, because there is no difference between emphasizing the content of a nominal sentence and emphasizing a verbal sentence.

It has also been said: the underlying form is ﴿fa-al-ḥaqqu al-ḥaqqu﴾, meaning: "I will do it." Ibn 'Abbās, Mujāhid, and al-A'mash read both words in the nominative (raf'), so the first is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is omitted. It has been said that its estimated form is ﴿fa-al-ḥaqqu anā﴾ (so the truth is I), and it has been said: ﴿fa-al-ḥaqqu minnī﴾ (so the truth is from me), and it has been said: its estimated form is ﴿fa-al-ḥaqqu qasamī﴾ (so the truth is my oath), and it was omitted just as it was omitted in "la'amruka la-aqūmanna" (by your life, I will surely stand), and in "yamīnu Allāhi abraḥu qā'idan" (the oath of God, I will not leave while seated), meaning: "la'amruka qasamī" (by your life is my oath) and "yamīnu Allāhi qasamī" (the oath of God is my oath). This sentence is the sentence of the oath, and its response is ﴿la-amla'anna﴾.

As for ﴿wa-al-ḥaqqu aqūlu﴾, it is also a subject, whose predicate is the sentence, and the returning pronoun (al-'ā'id) was omitted, as in the reading of Ibn 'Abbās: ﴿wa-kullan wa'ada Allāhu al-ḥusnā﴾ [al-Nisā': 95] (And to each God has promised the best). Ibn 'Aṭiyya said: As for the first, it is raised by being the subject, and its predicate is in His saying ﴿la-amla'anna﴾, because the meaning is: "that I will fill." He ended there.

This is not correct, because ﴿la-amla'anna﴾ is the response of an oath, and it must be a sentence, so it cannot be interpreted as a single word (mufrad). Also, it is not a verbal noun estimated with a verbal particle and a verb so that it could be resolved into them. But since it was valid for him to attribute what was estimated to the subject, it was judged to be its predicate.

Al-Ḥasan, 'Īsā, and 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Ḥammād, from Abū Bakr, read both words in the genitive (jarr). This can be explained as: the first is governed by an omitted oath particle (wāw al-qasam), its estimated form being ﴿fa-wa-al-ḥaqqi wa-al-ḥaqqi﴾ (so by the truth and the truth), and the second is conjoined to it, as you say: "wa-Allāhi wa-Allāhi la-aqūmanna" (by God, by God, I will surely stand). And ﴿aqūlu﴾ is an interjection (i'tirāḍ) between the oath and its response.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: ﴿wa-al-ḥaqqa aqūlu﴾: that is, "I say nothing except the truth," in the manner of quoting the wording of the thing sworn by. Its meaning is emphasis and affirmation (tawkīd and tasdīd). This aspect is permissible both for the accusative and the nominative, and it is a subtle and good aspect. He ended there.

Its summary is that he made the verb "say" operate on the wording of the thing sworn by, by way of quotation, whether in the accusative, nominative, or genitive. Mujāhid and al-A'mash, with a variant from them both; Abān ibn Taghlib; Ṭalḥa in one narration; Ḥamza, 'Āṣim (according to al-Mufaḍḍal), Khalaf, and al-'Absī read ﴿fa-al-ḥaqqu﴾ in the nominative and ﴿wa-al-ḥaqqa﴾ in the accusative, and their i'rāb (grammatical analysis) has already been mentioned.

The apparent meaning is that His saying ﴿ajma'īna﴾ (all) is an emphasis for the one spoken about and the one conjoined to it, which is the pronoun of Iblīs and whoever is conjoined to him, meaning: "from you and from those who follow you, all of them." Al-Zamakhsharī permitted that ﴿ajma'īna﴾ be an emphasis for the pronoun in ﴿minhum﴾ (from among them) which is implied, meaning: "I will surely fill Jahannam with the devils and with whoever followed them from all of mankind, with no difference in that between one person and another, after the existence of followers among them from the descendants of the prophets and others." He ended there.

The pronoun in ﴿'alayhi﴾ (upon it) refers to the Qur'an, as said by Ibn 'Abbās. It has also been said that it refers to the revelation (waḥy), and it has been said that it refers to the call to God (al-du'ā' ilā Allāh).

﴿wa-mā anā mina al-mutakallifīn﴾ (and I am not of those who impose): that is, those who affect what they are not of, adorning themselves with what is not theirs, so that I would claim prophethood and speak on behalf of God.

﴿in huwa﴾ (it is not), that is, the Qur'an, ﴿illā dhikrun﴾ (except a reminder): that is, from God, ﴿li-al-'ālamīn﴾ (to the worlds): the two weighty creatures, mankind and jinn.

﴿wa-la-ta'lamunna naba'ahu﴾ (and you will surely know its news): that is, the final outcome of its report for whoever believed in it and whoever turned away from it. ﴿ba'da ḥīn﴾ (after a time). Ibn 'Abbās, 'Ikrima, and Ibn Zayd said: it means the Day of Resurrection. Qatāda, al-Farrā', and al-Zajjāj said: after death. Al-Ḥasan used to say: "O son of Adam, at death the certain news (al-khabar al-yaqīn) will come to you." It has also been said: the meaning is that the reality of what I say will become clear to you.

﴿ba'da ḥīn﴾: that is, in the near future, when the swords of the Muslims seize you, and that was the Battle of Badr. Al-Suddī indicated this.

* *

Sūrat al-Zumar: seventy-five verses, Meccan.

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. ﴿The revelation of the Book is from God, the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾ [al-Zumar: 1]. ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, so worship God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-Zumar: 2]. ﴿Unquestionably, to God belongs sincere religion. And those who take protectors other than Him, [say], "We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to God in position." Indeed, God will judge between them concerning that over which they differ. Indeed, God does not guide one who is a liar and [continually] ungrateful﴾ [al-Zumar: 3]. ﴿Had God intended to take a son, He would have chosen from what He creates whatever He wills. Exalted is He. He is God, the One, the Subduer﴾ [al-Zumar: 4]. ﴿He created the heavens and the earth in truth. He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term. Unquestionably, He is the Almighty, the Forgiving﴾ [al-Zumar: 5]. ﴿He created you from one soul; then He made from it its mate, and He sent down for you eight kinds of livestock. He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, in three darknesses. That is God, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion. There is no deity except Him, so how are you turned away?﴾ [al-Zumar: 6]. ﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed God is free of need of you, and He does not approve for His servants disbelief; but if you are grateful, He approves it for you. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the chests﴾ [al-Zumar: 7]. ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance. Then when He bestows upon him a favor from Him, he forgets what he had been calling to before and sets up rivals to God to mislead [others] from His way. Say, "Enjoy your disbelief for a little; indeed, you are of the companions of the Fire"﴾ [al-Zumar: 8]. ﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient during periods of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord [like one who does not]? Say, "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?" Only they will be reminded who are people of understanding﴾ [al-Zumar: 9]. ﴿Say, "O My servants who have believed, fear your Lord. For those who do good in this world is good, and the earth of God is spacious. Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account"﴾ [al-Zumar: 10]. ﴿Say, "Indeed, I have been commanded to worship God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-Zumar: 11]. ﴿And I have been commanded to be the first of the Muslims﴾ [al-Zumar: 12]. ﴿Say, "Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a great Day"﴾ [al-Zumar: 13]. ﴿Say, "It is God I worship, sincere to Him in my religion﴾ [al-Zumar: 14]. ﴿So worship what you will besides Him." Say, "Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss"﴾ [al-Zumar: 15]. ﴿For them will be layers of fire above them and layers below them. That is what God frightens His servants with. O My servants, then fear Me﴾ [al-Zumar: 16]. ﴿And those who avoid the false gods, not worshipping them, and turn back to God—for them is good news. So give good tidings to My servants﴾ [al-Zumar: 17]. ﴿Those who listen to speech and follow the best of it. Those are the ones whom God has guided, and those are the people of understanding﴾ [al-Zumar: 18]. ﴿Then is one upon whom the word of punishment has come [to be deserved]—would you, then, save one who is in the Fire?﴾ [al-Zumar: 19]. ﴿But those who fear their Lord will have lofty chambers, above which are built chambers, beneath which rivers flow. [It is] the promise of God; God does not fail in His promise﴾ [al-Zumar: 20]. ﴿Have you not seen that God sends down rain from the sky and makes it flow as springs in the earth, then brings out by it crops of varying colors? Then it dries, and you see it turn yellow; then He makes it crumbled debris. Indeed, in that is a reminder for those of understanding﴾ [al-Zumar: 21]. ﴿So is one whose breast God has expanded to Islam and who is upon light from his Lord [like one whose heart is hardened]? Woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of God. Those are in manifest error﴾ [al-Zumar: 22]. ﴿God has sent down the best statement, a Book consistent and repeated; the skins shiver therefrom of those who fear their Lord; then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of God. That is the guidance of God; He guides thereby whom He wills. And whom God leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾ [al-Zumar: 23]. ﴿Then is one who shields his face with his face from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection [like one who is safe]? And it will be said to the wrongdoers, "Taste what you used to earn"﴾ [al-Zumar: 24]. ﴿Those before them denied, and the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive﴾ [al-Zumar: 25]. ﴿So God made them taste disgrace in the life of this world, but the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew﴾ [al-Zumar: 26]. ﴿And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example that they might be reminded﴾ [al-Zumar: 27]. ﴿An Arabic Qur'an, without any crookedness, that they might fear God﴾ [al-Zumar: 28]. ﴿God presents an example: a man in whom are [several] partners disputing with one another, and a man belonging exclusively to one man. Are they equal in comparison? Praise is to God; but most of them do not know﴾ [al-Zumar: 29]. ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die﴾ [al-Zumar: 30]. ﴿Then indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord you will dispute﴾ [al-Zumar: 31].

[p. 413] Al-Takwīr: wrapping and coiling. It is said: "kāra al-'imāmata 'alā ra'sihi wa-kawwarahā" (he wound the turban on his head). "Khawwalahu al-ni'mata" means: he gave him a favor at the outset, without any reward; and "khawwala" is not used for a recompense. Zuhayr said:
"There, if they are given wealth as a favor, they are given [wealth] as a favor" (wording variant: "yustakhyalū al-māla yukhayyalū").
Abū al-Najm said:
"He gave and did not withhold, and did not make others withhold; a heap of the summits from the favored property of the bestower."

Hāja al-zar'u: it rose from its roots; it is said: it dried up. Al-ḥuṭām: the crumbs after its dryness. Al-qush'arīra: the contraction of the skin; it is said: "iqsha'arra jiluduhu min al-khawf" (his skin shivered from fear): his hair stood up, and it is a proverb for intense fear. Al-shikāsa: bad character and its difficulty.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 38, verses 67–88 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Say: It is a great news.﴾ ﴿You turn away from it.﴾ ﴿I had no knowledge of the Exalted Assembly when they disputed.﴾ ﴿It is only revealed to me that I am a clear warner.﴾ ﴿When your Lord said to the angels: I am creating a human from clay.﴾ ﴿So when I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down prostrate before him.﴾ ﴿So the angels prostrated, all of them together.﴾ ﴿Except Iblis; he was arrogant and was among the disbelievers.﴾ ﴿He said: O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My two hands? Were you arrogant, or were you among the exalted?﴾ ﴿He said: I am better than him; You created me from fire and You created him from clay.﴾ ﴿He said: Then get out of it, for you are accursed.﴾ ﴿And indeed My curse is upon you until the Day of Recompense.﴾ ﴿He said: My Lord, then give me respite until the Day they are resurrected.﴾ ﴿He said: Then you are among those given respite.﴾ ﴿Until the Day of the appointed time.﴾ ﴿He said: By Your might, I will surely mislead them all.﴾ ﴿Except Your sincere servants among them.﴾ ﴿He said: Then the truth, and I say the truth.﴾ ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you and with whoever follows you of them, all together.﴾ ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any wage for it, and I am not of the pretenders.﴾ ﴿It is only a reminder to the worlds.﴾ ﴿And you will surely know its news after a time.﴾.

The pronoun in His saying ﴿Say: It is a great news﴾ refers to what he had informed of: that he is a messenger warning and calling to Allah, and that He, exalted is He, is the One alone in divinity, characterized by those attributes of oneness, dominion, sovereignty over the world, might and forgiveness. It is a great report, from which none turns away except a heedless person who is extremely heedless.

Ibn Abbas said: "the great news" is the Qur'an. Al-Hasan said: it is the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: it is the story of Adam, and the informing of it without having heard it from anyone.

The author of al-Tahrir said: the context and apparent meaning of the verse indicate that by His saying ﴿Say: It is a great news﴾ He means what Allah related of the dispute of the people of the Fire and the arguing of the followers with the leaders, because it is among the conditions of the resurrection, and the Quraysh used to deny the resurrection, the reckoning and the punishment, and they were turning away from that.

His saying ﴿I had no knowledge of the Exalted Assembly when they disputed﴾ is an argument against the Quraysh that what he brought is from Allah and not from himself. Indeed, whoever is on earth has no knowledge of whoever is in heaven except by Allah's informing; and knowledge of the unseen cannot be reached except by Allah's informing. His knowledge of the conditions of the people of the Fire and the beginning of the creation of Adam was not from himself; so his informing of that is by Allah's informing. The evidence is the story of Adam, because he was the first human created, and between him and the Messenger, peace be upon him, there were long ages and bygone generations. End of the quotation, and at its end there is some abridgment.

Then he argued for the authenticity of his prophethood: that what he reports about the Exalted Assembly and their disputing is a matter of which he had no knowledge at all. Then he came to know it from a route other than the one by which learners acquire knowledge; rather, that is derived from revelation. The phrase "with the assembly" (bi-l-mala') is related to "knowledge" ('ilm), and "when" (idh) is in the accusative governed by it. Al-Zamakhshari said: it is related to a deleted element, because the meaning is: I had no knowledge of the speech of the Exalted Assembly at the time of their disputing.

"When he said" (idh qala) is a substitute (badal) for "when they dispute" (idh yakhtasimun) regarding the Exalted Assembly, who are the angels. Whoever said they are the Quraysh is further from correct. The disputing of the angels concerned the matter of Adam and his offspring, in placing them on the earth. They said: ﴿Will You place therein one who causes corruption therein?﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:30]. Ibn Abbas said: and al-Hasan said: Indeed Allah creates a creation that we were nobler than and more knowledgeable than. It was also said: it concerned the expiations and forgiveness of sins; for when a servant does a good deed, the angels differ about the measure of its reward in that, until Allah decides as He wills. And in a hadith: "His Lord said to him in his sleep, peace be upon him: 'About what do they dispute?' I said: 'I do not know.' He said: 'About the expiations, and about perfecting the ablution in hardships, and about walking the steps to the congregations.'"

Al-Zamakhshari said: the speaking between Allah, glory be to Him, and the other was through an angel, and the actual speaker was the intermediary angel. So it is valid that the speaking was between the angels and Adam and Iblis, and they are the Exalted Assembly.

The meaning of the disputing is speaking back and forth. It was said: the Exalted Assembly are the angels, and the pronoun in ﴿when they dispute﴾ refers to the disbelieving Arabs, some of whom say: they are the daughters of Allah, and some say: they are gods that are worshipped, and other statements of theirs.

﴿It is only revealed to me﴾, i.e., only what is revealed to me; ﴿that I am a warner﴾, i.e., for warning. He omitted the preposition (lam), and joined the verb to its object, the passive form. The pronoun may be implied by the meaning: i.e., "It is revealed to me" refers to it, meaning: only the warning is revealed, and "to me" is put in its place. It may also be that "innama" is the passive subject: i.e., only the warning is revealed to me. Abu Ja'far read ﴿illa innama﴾ with a kasra on the hamza of innama, as a reported speech (hikaya): meaning, only this sentence is revealed to me, as if it were said to him: "You are a clear warner," and he related the meaning. This is like a person saying: "I am knowledgeable," and it is said to him: "You said that you are knowledgeable," so the meaning is reported.

Al-Zamakhshari said: It was also read innama with a kasra as reported speech, i.e., only this statement, which is that I say to you ﴿Indeed I am a clear warner﴾, so I do not claim anything else. End of quotation.

In his explanation there is a contradiction, for he said "i.e., only this statement," which apparently is the sentence ﴿Indeed I am a clear warner﴾, then he said: "which is that I say to you," so the position is that of the subject, namely "that I say to you," and "that" and what follows are in the accusative position. According to his statement "only this statement," it would be in the nominative position, so they conflict.

It has been mentioned that "when he said" is a substitute for "when they dispute," this being if the dispute was about the one who will be made successor on earth; but according to other statements it would be in the accusative governed by "mention" (udhkur).

Since the Quraysh opposed the Messenger, peace be upon him, out of envy and arrogance, He mentioned the situation of Iblis, who opposed the command of Allah out of envy and arrogance, and what he came to of cursing and expulsion from the mercy of Allah, so that whoever has some trait of these two would be deterred from that.

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you say: how was it valid for Him to say to them ﴿Indeed I am creating a human﴾, when they did not know what a human is and had not been acquainted with it before? I say: its explanation is that He had said to them: "Indeed I am creating a creation of such and such a description," but when He related it He limited Himself to the name. End of quotation.

The human (bashar) is Adam, peace be upon him. Here He mentions that He created him from clay; and in Al 'Imran: ﴿He created him from dust﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:59]; in al-Hijr: ﴿from dry clay of black molded mud﴾ [al-Hijr 15:26]; and in al-Anbiya': ﴿from haste﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:37]. There is no contradiction, since the remote substance is dust, then what follows it, which is clay, then what follows it, which is black molded mud, then the substance that follows the mud, which is dry clay. As for ﴿from haste﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:37], its explanation has already passed.

﴿So when I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down prostrate before him.﴾ ﴿So the angels prostrated, all of them together.﴾ ﴿Except Iblis﴾: the discussion of this has already been covered in al-Hijr. Here ﴿he was arrogant and was among the disbelievers﴾, [p. 410] and in al-Baqarah: ﴿He refused and was arrogant and was among the disbelievers﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:34]; in al-A'raf: ﴿He was not among those who prostrate﴾ [al-A'raf 7:11]; in al-Hijr: ﴿He refused to be with those who prostrate﴾ [al-Hijr 15:31]; in al-Isra': ﴿He said: Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?﴾ [al-Isra' 17:61]; and in al-Kahf: ﴿He was of the jinn and defied the command of his Lord﴾ [al-Kahf 18:50].

The exception in all these verses indicates that he did not prostrate. Sometimes it is emphasized with pure negation; sometimes his refusal to prostrate is mentioned, which is his disdain for that; and sometimes it is stated explicitly that this refusal was caused by arrogance. The apparent meaning is that His saying ﴿and was among the disbelievers﴾ means his disbelief at that time, even if he had not been a disbeliever before; and it is conjoined to "was arrogant," which strengthens this, because the arrogance about prostration only occurred to him at the time of the command.

It is also possible that it is information from Him about his disbelief having preceded in past times in the knowledge of Allah.

﴿He said: O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating﴾. In al-A'raf: ﴿What prevented you from not prostrating﴾ [al-A'raf 7:12]. This indicates that "an tasjuda" here shows that "la" in ﴿an la aqula﴾ [al-A'raf 7:105] is extra; and the meaning also indicates this, because He only asks about what prevented him from prostrating, and this is a question of confirmation and rebuke. As for "li-ma khalaqtu" [what I created], those who permit applying "ma" to individuals who have intellect have used it as evidence, and they interpreted "ma" here as a verbal noun (masdariyyah), and the verbal noun is intended to mean the created thing, not the literal verbal noun.

Al-Jahdari read ﴿lamma﴾ with a fatha on the lam and a shadda on the mim, ﴿khalaqtu bi-yadayya﴾ in the singular; the majority read it in the dual. It is also read ﴿biyadayya﴾ like the reading ﴿bi-musrikhiyya﴾ [Ibrahim 14:22]. He, exalted is He, also said: ﴿of what Our hands have done﴾ [Ya Sin 36:71] in the plural. All of these are expressions for power and strength; and He expressed it with "hand," since it is customary among humans that seizing and strength are by the hand.

Al-Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-Tayyib held that the hand is an attribute of essence (sifat dhat). Ibn Atiyya said: this is an opinion that is disliked.

The majority read ﴿asta'kbarta﴾ with the interrogative hamza, so "am" is a connected "am" that is equivalent to the hamza. Ibn Atiyya said: many grammarians held that "am" is not equivalent to the alif when the two verbs differ; it is only equivalent when both are attached to one verb, like your saying: "Did Zayd stand or 'Amr?" and "Did Zayd stand or 'Amr?" When the verbs differ, as in this verse, it is not equivalent. The meaning of the verse is: Has arrogance now come to you, or were you formerly one for whom it is not fitting to be commanded with such, because of the height of your station? This is by way of rebuke. End of quotation.

What he mentioned from many grammarians is an incorrect doctrine. Sibawayh said: you say "Did you strike Zayd or did you kill him?" Beginning here with the verb is better, because you are only asking about one of them, not knowing which of them occurred, and you are not asking about the position of one of them, as if you said: "Which of those occurred?" End of quotation. So he made "am" equivalent to the alif even though the two verbs differ.
